# Surface failed updates from the Identity API /manage/2fa endpoint

- [x] You've read the [Contributor Guide](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).
- [x] You've included unit or integration tests for your change, where applicable.
- [x] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [x] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making. If you'd like to propose a new feature or change, please open an issue to discuss the change or find an existing issue.

## Description

The `/manage/2fa` handler registered by `MapIdentityApi` ignored the `IdentityResult` returned by `SetTwoFactorEnabledAsync` and `ResetAuthenticatorKeyAsync`, and treated a `null` result from `GenerateNewTwoFactorRecoveryCodesAsync` as "no new codes". When the user update failed (for example an EF Core optimistic concurrency conflict caused by a concurrent update to the same user), the tracked user entity still held the modified values, so the endpoint returned HTTP 200 with a shared key, 2FA state or recovery codes that were never persisted.

Changes in `IdentityApiEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions`:

- Every `SetTwoFactorEnabledAsync` and `ResetAuthenticatorKeyAsync` call is checked, including the reset that initializes a missing authenticator key. A failure is returned as a validation problem built from the `IdentityResult` (e.g. `ConcurrencyFailure`), the same way the other endpoints in this file already handle failed results.
- A `null` result from `GenerateNewTwoFactorRecoveryCodesAsync` returns a `RecoveryCodeGenerationFailed` validation problem instead of HTTP 200 with `recoveryCodes: null`.

A successful response is now only built after every update in the request has been persisted. The response shape for successful requests is unchanged, and there are no public API changes.

Behavior change to call out: a request that previously got HTTP 200 while its update silently failed now gets HTTP 400. If the request changes more than one setting (for example `ResetSharedKey`, which disables 2FA and then resets the key), the steps that succeeded before the failure stay saved, the same as before this change. The client is now told that the request failed and can retry it.

## Tests

Added `TwoFactorReturnsValidationProblemWhenUserUpdateFails` to `MapIdentityApiTests`. It uses a `UserManager` whose user updates can be made to fail with `ConcurrencyFailure`, and verifies that:

- initializing the missing shared key, `ResetSharedKey`, `ResetRecoveryCodes` and `Enable` each return a 400 validation problem while updates fail, and
- once updates succeed again, the stored shared key, 2FA state and recovery code count are unchanged.

The test fails without the fix (the first request returns 200). All `Identity.FunctionalTests` pass locally.

Fixes #69941

Issues.Title: POC: General lazy HTTP/1.1 request-header values
Issues.Body:
# POC: General lazy HTTP/1.1 request-header values

- [x] Read the Contributor Guide and Code of Conduct.
- [x] Included targeted unit and hosted regression coverage.
- [x] Included experiment documentation and reproducible commands.
- [x] Open tracking issue: #69962.

## Description

**Discussion draft, not a shipping recommendation.** HTTP/1.1 is the protocol restriction, not a User-Agent-only restriction. The current implementation generalizes ordinary known and unknown **values**. Names remain eager. The earlier User-Agent experiment and its measured results are historical, not evidence for this new implementation. **Generalized Crank comparisons are pending.**

### Hypothesis and implementation

Can deferring changing unread values improve HTTP/1.1 workloads beyond existing known-name and stable-value reuse, without unacceptable read/default-off or retained-memory costs?

The new default-off `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Experimental.LazyRequestHeaders` switch enables the explicit HTTP/1.1 ingress only; it does not silently broaden/alias the historical `LazyUserAgent` switch. HTTP/1.0, HPACK/QPACK, HTTP/2/HTTP/3 literal ingestion and trailers stay eager. Shared layout/accessor costs are still real.

One collection-owned byte arena grows geometrically up to 4096 bytes, with an aggregate copied-byte budget including discarded holes. Generated known slots and a single authoritative case-insensitive unknown dictionary carry decoded-or-range values. No borrowed input slices, raw placeholders or competing unknown sidecars. Names retain eager validation and existing interning. Host, Content-Length, Connection and Transfer-Encoding remain eager for host/framing/keep-alive processing.

Value reads materialize once; presence queries do not. Set/remove/reset discard unread values without decoding, clearing sensitive bytes. Growth clears the old buffer. Duplicate occurrences materialize the first value and append in order. Empty remains present. Non-ASCII, custom selectors, oversize and budget exhaustion fall back to eager decoding; validation/errors remain at ingestion. Decoded stable known strings retain reuse.

### Alternatives and tradeoffs

Existing stable-known reuse is the baseline, not an always-allocating strawman. Response raw serialization is not request-buffer ownership. Borrowed pipe/parser buffers are unsafe without a lifetime redesign; lazy names and consumer hints are deferred. No ignored-header/public API contract is introduced.

Copying, scanning, clearing, per-known-slot metadata, larger unknown entries, retained capacity and first-read/default-off costs require measurement. The arena budget is an untuned hypothesis. Public prior art #38585/#42681 concerns reuse correctness; #31492 concerns known-header memory/coverage; #27467 typed APIs. None proves a lazy-allocation win.

### Current generalized correctness

- **9317 Core header/parser/HTTP/1 cases pass**, including fresh independent value-reader paths across eligible known names, unknown X-Example and typed-unknown Alt-Svc, on/off; ownership, duplicates, mutation without decoding, presence, empty/missing, arena growth/exact budget/fallback/secret clearing, encoding/validation, reset/reuse, CopyTo argument errors and eager controls.
- **777 HTTP/2/HTTP/3/hosted cases pass, five platform/TLS skips**, including fragmented 255/256/257-byte known/unknown values, body reads before access, keep-alive reuse, eager HTTP/1.0 and HTTP/2/QPACK compatibility, and switch-enabled Host/Content-Length rejection.
- Two earlier broad functional runs each failed a different existing asynchronous test. Both cases plus new hosted cases then passed together, followed by the passing full selection. Failed logs remain; no cause is inferred or failure hidden by the repeat. Private-layout reflection probes preserve their original pooled-reference clearing assertions.
- Frozen generalized source **`96def7878b6e2ff7fb5f1afd73e54b4be35c103d`** passes the broader 777-case functional selection again and **96 real-socket requests** (12 processes, eight requests per persistent connection), exact body/length/checksum, with actual local Core identity verified. [Current methodology and source](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/perfboss/lazy-user-agent-poc/src/Servers/Kestrel/perf/LazyHeaders/README.md). Full per-file manifests and matched binaries are preserved with the evidence.

### Generalized end-to-end methodology

The expanded fixed-length fixture sends stable/changing Accept, Accept-Language, User-Agent, X-Example and X-Request-Nonce. Modes: ignore/read-one/read-all/enumerate, known/unknown duplicates and budget fallback. Socket checks assert actual body, observed length and checksum, not only value counts.

Required primary comparison: five rotating/interleaved repeats of stable/changing x ignore/read-all x baseline/head-off/head-on. Original net12 runtime, identical application/dependencies/server GC, replacing only baseline Core DLL; full payload manifests, loaded binary/runtime identities, raw counters, latencies, errors and failed attempts retained. Local shared two-core loopback is diagnostic evidence, not an isolated server ceiling. Allocation rates are not bytes/request; no MAX-rate/total-request arithmetic.

Three initial generalized pilots had positive metrics and zero errors. The first full-duration baseline run reported **seven socket timeouts**, zero bad responses, 1,192,592 requests; its guard stopped the plan. All evidence and traceback are retained. After a separately tested CopyTo argument-compatibility correction, the frozen-head plan records socket errors in **all predetermined cases without filtering/replacement**; bad responses or missing measurements still fail. This is an explicit stopping-policy change, not a clean-run claim or a client-settings change. Corrected-head comparisons remain pending.

### Historical evidence preserved

At `112166c827fbc38e88f4327675964de15a4470d0`, the **User-Agent-only** 60-run comparison completed 70,130,567 requests with zero bad/socket errors. Changing/ignored median allocation rate was 14.89/14.59/10.35 MB/s base/off/on, with overlapping throughput spreads and read/default-off concerns. Nine separate single-repeat supplements retain 15 baseline enumeration timeouts; an earlier default-off attempt retains 16 timeouts. None is replaced or presented as generalized performance evidence.

[Historical raw artifacts and hashes](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/tree/112166c827fbc38e88f4327675964de15a4470d0/src/Servers/Kestrel/perf/LazyHeaders/crank-local). Existing branch `perfboss/lazy-user-agent-poc` is retained to preserve continuity.

## Remaining work

The generalized source/checks and matched workload are published. Complete and publish its comparative Crank evidence, then discuss read/default-off and retained-memory budgets. Cold/low-reuse and isolated client/server follow-ups remain explicit limitations before any shipping recommendation. No overall win is claimed.

Issues.Title: Apply MapStaticAssets conventions to the runtime fallback endpoint
Issues.Body:
# Apply MapStaticAssets conventions to the runtime fallback endpoint

- [x] You've read the [Contributor Guide](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).
- [x] You've included unit or integration tests for your change, where applicable.
- [x] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [x] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making. If you'd like to propose a new feature or change, please open an issue to discuss the change or find an existing issue.

## Description

When the app runs from build output, `MapStaticAssets()` also registers a runtime fallback endpoint (`{**path:file}`) that serves files added to the web root after the build. Conventions added to the builder returned by `MapStaticAssets()` (for example `RequireAuthorization()`) were only applied to the manifest endpoints, so files reached through the fallback were served without that endpoint metadata.

This implements the selected approach (A) from the issue:

- `StaticAssetsEndpointConventionBuilder` gets an internal `AttachFallback(IEndpointConventionBuilder)`. `Add` and `Finally` now also forward each convention to every attached fallback builder. The attached fallbacks are snapshotted under the existing lock and invoked outside it.
- `StaticAssetDevelopmentRuntimeHandler.EnableSupport` attaches the fallback after the fallback's own conventions (file-exists constraint, GET/HEAD restriction) are added. Internal conventions added before that point (runtime patching) are not forwarded; conventions added by the app after `MapStaticAssets()` returns are.
- Calling `MapStaticAssets()` more than once for the same manifest returns the same builder and registers another fallback, so forwarding reaches every attached fallback. In that case the internal runtime patching convention from the second call is added after the first fallback is attached, so `AttachRuntimePatching` now skips endpoints without a `StaticAssetDescriptor` instead of throwing.

Because authorization and other metadata are evaluated for the fallback endpoint before the file is resolved, the result does not depend on how the request path is spelled.

No public API changes. Behavior with `DisableStaticAssetNotFoundRuntimeFallback=true` or a global `FallbackPolicy` is unchanged.

Behavior change to call out: apps that relied on the fallback being unaffected by conventions (for example, serving newly added files anonymously while manifest assets require authorization) will now see those conventions applied to the fallback too. A user convention that assumes manifest-specific metadata (for example `Metadata.OfType<StaticAssetDescriptor>().Single()`) will now also run against the fallback endpoint. I can follow up with a docs/breaking change note if this is considered a breaking change.

## Tests

Added to `StaticAssetsIntegrationTests`:

- `ConventionsAreAppliedToRuntimeFallbackEndpoints`: `Add` and `Finally` conventions reach both fallback endpoints when `MapStaticAssets()` is called twice, as well as the manifest endpoint.
- `RequireAuthorizationIsAppliedToRuntimeFallbackEndpoint`: with `RequireAuthorization()`, a manifest asset and a file added after startup both return 401.

Both tests fail without the fix (the fallback request returns 200).

Fixes #69754

Issues.Title: Harden skill-evals CI workflow and update Vally dependency
Issues.Body:
A few improvements to `eng/skill-evals`:
1. **Move the `chmod +x` fixture step out of eval specs and into `stage_run.ps1`.** Today `commands: [chmod +x .eval-gh/gh]` lives in individual `eval.vally.yaml` files; moving it into the trusted staging script lets us stop allowing arbitrary `commands`/`mcpServers`/executor overrides in per-eval specs going forward, with no change in behavior for existing evals.

2. **Reject unexpected fields in staged eval specs** (`commands`, `mcpServers`, custom `executor.config.provider`, etc.) as part of staging, so only the documented/expected shape is accepted.

3. **Bump the pinned [`@microsoft/vally-cli`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/vally) version** (currently 0.14.0) to pick up newer features, including the built-in Docker execution backend (0.18.0+) for better process isolation if we want to use it later.

Why: these are low-risk cleanups that tighten what a skill-eval spec is allowed to do and keep the pinned tooling current, without affecting any existing eval behavior.

Issues.Title: Fix ErrorBoundary exception routing for non-component event receivers
Issues.Body:
## Description

Fixes exceptions from non-component event receivers, such as non-rendering
`EventUtil` handlers, bypassing the enclosing `ErrorBoundary`.

## Root Cause

`Renderer.DispatchEventAsync` uses the callback receiver's component state
to route exceptions. Non-component receivers have no component state, so
their exceptions are treated as unhandled.

## Output

### Before

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec0b9233-3663-468c-bacf-298c3675e290

### After

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49b8d29d-e38d-4e0a-8ea0-b620a0e6fc15

## Fix Details

- Use the rendering component's state for error routing when the callback
  receiver isn't a component.
- Preserve component-receiver behavior and pending-task ownership.

## Tests

Adds E2E coverage for synchronous and asynchronous non-rendering event
exceptions, including an asynchronous exception after component removal.

Fixes dotnet/aspnetcore#69765

Issues.Title: Design Proposal: MarkupString JSON Round-Trip Support
Issues.Body:
## Summary This proposal addresses [dotnet/aspnetcore#67608](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67608) by adding `[JsonConstructor]` to the existing `MarkupString(string value)` constructor. The annotation selects the existing immutable-value constructor during `System.Text.Json` deserialization so applications can restore the string from the existing object-shaped JSON representation. No new constructor, mutable property, converter, or registration API is proposed. Serialization retains the object containing `Value`; direct construction, conversion, default construction, and rendering remain unchanged. **Design recommendation:** Retain the constructor annotation, subject to compatibility characterization and maintainer acceptance. This is not formal ASP.NET Core API approval. **Readiness:** Suitable for design discussion. API-shape suitability is not runtime verification, maintainer acceptance, or release approval. All implementation acceptance checks remain pending. ## Motivation and Goals ### Audience and scenarios - **Audience:** End-application developers serializing models containing `MarkupString`; component-library authors also benefit. - **Commonality:** Happy-path correctness for applications already serializing models containing this type, not a requirement for every Blazor application. Ordinary rendering does not require JSON serialization. - **Environments:** The same managed contract applies to Server, WebAssembly, and applications referencing the Components assembly. Source-generated metadata matters for trimmed/AOT consumers. Render mode, circuit count, and deployment topology do not determine constructor selection. - **Dominant scenario:** Preserve an existing model property's string, originating from stored application content or an in-memory model, through an object-shaped `System.Text.Json` round trip. Direct and collection values are adjacent cases. Bare-string representations and dictionary keys are separate requirements. - **Justification:** The existing public constructor already represents the complete value. A constructor-selection attribute addresses the reported scenario without adding methods, properties, or framework configuration. ### Problem `MarkupString` is a `readonly struct` with: - An existing public constructor, `MarkupString(string value)`. - A public getter-only `Value` property. - An explicit conversion from `string`. - A `ToString()` override. Serialization can read `Value`, but the constructor is not marked with `[JsonConstructor]`. Under the documented `System.Text.Json` rules for structs, deserialization does not select this parameterized constructor automatically. Default construction cannot populate a getter-only property, so the original string is not restored. The failure is lost round-trip data, not necessarily an exception from `Deserialize`. The conversion operator and `ToString()` do not supply the JSON deserialization contract. The regression assertion must compare `restored.HtmlContent.Value` with the original string. Comparing the `MarkupString` struct directly with a `string`, or using `ToString()` alone, can obscure the actual contract. ### Use cases 1. **Application model round trip:** A model containing an HTML-content property is serialized, stored, and later restored without losing its string value. 2. **JSON-backed state:** An application-owned state object contains `MarkupString` values. The application expects JSON restoration to reconstruct those values. 3. **Collections and nested models:** The value appears inside a DTO, array, or dictionary rather than only as a top-level value. 4. **Trimmed or AOT application:** An application uses a source-generated `JsonSerializerContext` and expects the same value preservation as reflection-based serialization. These are serializer scenarios. This proposal does not claim that every Blazor persistence, JS interop, or render-mode transition has already been tested. ### Goals - Restore exact non-null strings through the actual framework type while preserving object-shaped serialization. - Support reflection and generated metadata, subject to execution evidence, without changing direct construction, conversion, default construction, or rendering. - Respect standard application converter/resolver customization. ## In Scope - Annotate the existing public string constructor with `[JsonConstructor]`. - Preserve the constructor body, parameter name/type/nullability, `readonly` modifier, getter, conversion operator, and `ToString()`. - Keep the existing assembly and namespace. - Reuse the built-in serializer contract; add no custom converter or registration API. - Add focused managed regression tests, generated-metadata coverage, compatibility characterization, and consumer-facing documentation. ### Expected file changes during implementation | File | Planned change | |---|---| | `src/Components/Components/src/MarkupString.cs` | Add the serialization namespace import and constructor attribute; preserve existing code otherwise. | | Existing Components managed test project | Add focused type round-trip and serializer-boundary tests, including source-generated metadata. Extend a matching class if present; otherwise use a type-specific class following nearby naming conventions. | | `src/Components/Components/src/PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` | Change only if repository API tooling requires a tracked metadata update; do not invent a new constructor signature. | | Existing Components sample/E2E assets | Use the canonical sample workflow for host validation; add or extend a small permanent host scenario where required by area policy. | | Consumer-facing API documentation | Explain default object-shaped JSON support and relevant option limitations. | ## Out of Scope - Bare-string JSON, dictionary-key support, and Newtonsoft.Json support. - Null normalization, a constructor null guard, or changed parameter nullability. - Recovery when serializer options omit the value, or guarantees for every custom contract. - Changes to JS interop, persistence protocols, render-mode transfer, renderer behavior, or JavaScript. - New packages, package-manifest changes, NuGet configuration changes, and SDK configuration changes. - Selecting a servicing release or claiming trimmed, Native AOT, or WebAssembly AOT deployment support without separate validation. ## Risks and Unknowns - **Observable default-behavior change:** Valid object-shaped input will restore content instead of yielding a default-valued struct. Strict options and incompatible member values can introduce new deserialization errors. - **Constructor binding becomes part of the contract:** Future constructor or property changes must preserve the parameter-to-property match. - **Null and missing differ from empty:** Tests must inspect `Value`; `ToString()` normalizes null to empty and can conceal data loss. - **Omitted data cannot be recovered:** Naming, ignore settings, or custom contracts can prevent content from being supplied. The annotation does not override application customization. - **Validation is still required:** Reflection tests do not prove generated-metadata behavior. Generated-metadata execution does not prove trimming, Native AOT, or browser WebAssembly AOT deployment. - **Release placement is undecided:** Maintainers must accept measured compatibility differences and identify the target release. No backport is implied. ## API Surface ### Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.MarkupString - Add `[JsonConstructor]` to the existing public `MarkupString(string value)` constructor. - Add no public signatures and remove none. Preserve all other members and the existing assembly/namespace. - Apply API baseline changes only if repository tooling requires them; do not re-list an unchanged constructor as a new signature. **Why:** Constructor-based deserialization is the existing mechanism for immutable structs. The constructor parameter `value` already matches the CLR property `Value` by name, case-insensitively, and by type. Selecting that constructor restores the value without making the struct mutable or introducing a second JSON implementation. Proposed reference-surface metadata delta: ```diff namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components { public readonly struct MarkupString { + [System.Text.Json.Serialization.JsonConstructorAttribute] public MarkupString(string value); } } ``` Only the affected member is shown; all other members remain unchanged. ### JSON contract The logical default JSON shape remains: ```json { "HtmlContent": { "Value": "
Example content
" } } ``` Actual JSON text may escape HTML characters under the selected encoder. Compare parsed structure and decoded values rather than one escaping spelling. With web/camel-case options, property names follow those options, for example `htmlContent` and `value`. Constructor-parameter matching to CLR properties is separate from JSON-name matching and does not enable case-insensitive JSON matching universally. A bare-string representation such as `{"HtmlContent":"
Example content
"}` is not the new default. During a round trip, serialization reads the existing getter, deserialization binds the JSON member to its property metadata, and the selected string constructor assigns `Value` through its unchanged body. ### Accessibility No new UI or DOM behavior is introduced. Existing rendering and accessibility behavior are unchanged; the observable contract is the restored managed string value. ### API review The constructor is already public, but its serializer metadata and default deserialization behavior change. Treat this as a potential API/behavioral contract change. - Include the attribute-only reference-surface delta in review material. - When opening an implementation PR, follow the repository process to create a separate API proposal issue linked to this originating issue and the implementation PR. - Implementation and merge need not wait for approval, but the final shape must be covered by `api-approved` before inclusion in an RTM release. - A passing API baseline is not API approval. Do not edit the shipped baseline merely to re-list an unchanged member. ## Edge Case Scenarios ### Compatibility impact | Area | Impact | |---|---| | Source and binary signatures | No constructor, member, operator, namespace, or assembly signature changes. | | Serialization output | Preserve the existing object shape and current naming/escaping options. | | Valid deserialization | Intentionally changes from losing the stored value to reconstructing it. | | Default construction | `default(MarkupString)` remains possible. Do not normalize its underlying null value to an empty string or add a constructor guard. | | Existing converters/resolvers | Continue using standard serializer customization and precedence. Do not override application configuration. | | Other serializers | No new Newtonsoft.Json or non-JSON support is promised by a `System.Text.Json` attribute. | | Dependencies | No new package should be needed; the Components assembly already contains `System.Text.Json` usage. Confirm with the normal build. | **This is not a claim of zero behavioral compatibility impact.** The following rows are design expectations to validate, not executed results. Inputs target a direct `MarkupString` unless stated otherwise. Ordinary options mean no custom converter/resolver, with `RespectRequiredConstructorParameters` and `RespectNullableAnnotations` both explicitly set to `false`. Each strict row changes only the named option. | Input or setting | Expected behavior after the change | Compatibility significance | |---|---|---| | `{"Value":"content"}` | Exact `"content"` value | Intended restoration instead of lost data. | | `{"Value":""}` | Empty string, not null | Separate regression; `ToString()` would hide the difference. | | `{"Value":null}` with ordinary options | Underlying `Value` is null | Preserve null semantics without a new guard. | | `{}` with ordinary options | Underlying `Value` is null | Missing content is not reconstructed. | | `{}` with `RespectRequiredConstructorParameters = true` and nullable enforcement disabled | Throw `JsonException` for the missing non-optional argument | Constructor selection introduces required-presence enforcement. | | `{"Value":null}` with `RespectNullableAnnotations = true` and required-parameter enforcement disabled | Throw `JsonException` for the non-nullable constructor parameter | Constructor selection introduces explicit-null enforcement. | | `{}` with `RespectNullableAnnotations = true` and required-parameter enforcement disabled | Underlying `Value` is null | Nullable enforcement alone does not require presence. | | Number, object, or array as `Value` | Reject incompatible member types | Characterize previously ignored input versus new rejection. | | Top-level JSON string | Reject under the built-in object contract | No bare-string schema is introduced. | | JSON `null` targeting `MarkupString` / `MarkupString?` | Reject / produce a nullable value with no value | Preserve ordinary value-type handling. | | Unknown member with ordinary unmapped-member handling | Follow normal serializer handling | No custom parsing policy. | | Naming and ignore options | Follow the configured contract | Do not promise restoration when content is omitted. | | Application-registered converter | Follow standard converter precedence | Validate a representative override, not every custom contract. | `RespectRequiredConstructorParameters` and `RespectNullableAnnotations` were introduced in .NET 9. Their respective `System.Text.Json.Serialization.RespectRequiredConstructorParametersDefault` and `System.Text.Json.Serialization.RespectNullableAnnotationsDefault` runtime feature switches can enable their defaults. Record runtime and serializer versions, effective option values, and relevant switches for validation. Nullable enforcement also applies during serialization. A default/null-valued `MarkupString` may already fail when its non-nullable getter is enforced. Characterize serialization independently so pre-existing failures are not attributed to the constructor annotation. Consumers that depended on default-valued results from otherwise valid JSON will observe the intended change. Do not weaken serializer options globally, change the constructor's nullability, or add an optional parameter to conceal these differences. Record actual results and obtain maintainer agreement on compatibility and release placement. ### Decisions requiring ownership | Decision | Required outcome | |---|---| | Compatibility and target release | Maintainer accepts the measured behavioral differences and identifies release placement. | | API approval | A separate proposal is linked to the originating issue and implementation PR; `api-approved` covers the final shape before RTM. | | Publish claims | Each claimed trimming/AOT deployment path has its own execution evidence. | | Final validation record | Exact commands, revisions, effective options, and per-case red/green or control results are recorded. | ## Examples ### Proposed framework change Keep the existing constructor body unchanged: ```csharp [JsonConstructor] public MarkupString(string value) { Value = value; } ``` The containing file would import `System.Text.Json.Serialization`. This snippet is a proposal, not a change already applied to the framework. ### Application round trip after the fix This example illustrates the intended contract; it has not been compiled or executed for this proposal. ```csharp using System; using System.Text.Json; using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components; var model = new ContentModel { HtmlContent = new MarkupString("
Example content
") }; var json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(model); var restored = JsonSerializer.Deserialize(json) ?? throw new JsonException("The content model was not restored."); if (restored.HtmlContent.Value != model.HtmlContent.Value) { throw new InvalidOperationException("Markup content did not round-trip."); } Console.WriteLine(restored.HtmlContent.Value); public sealed class ContentModel { public MarkupString HtmlContent { get; set; } } ``` Expected console output after the fix: ```text
Example content
``` For web defaults, pass `JsonSerializerOptions.Web` to both calls. The JSON uses camel-case member names while the restored value remains the same. ### Source-generated metadata example This is a separate example program: ```csharp using System; using System.Text.Json; using System.Text.Json.Serialization; using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components; var model = new ContentModel { HtmlContent = new MarkupString("

Source-generated round trip

") }; var json = JsonSerializer.Serialize( model, ContentJsonContext.Default.ContentModel); var restored = JsonSerializer.Deserialize( json, ContentJsonContext.Default.ContentModel) ?? throw new JsonException("The content model was not restored."); Console.WriteLine(restored.HtmlContent.Value); public sealed class ContentModel { public MarkupString HtmlContent { get; set; } } [JsonSourceGenerationOptions(GenerationMode = JsonSourceGenerationMode.Metadata)] [JsonSerializable(typeof(ContentModel))] internal sealed partial class ContentJsonContext : JsonSerializerContext { } ``` This example uses generated metadata for both directions. It does not itself disable reflection fallback; the validation consumer must do so explicitly. Compilation, runtime execution, and any claimed trimming, Native AOT, or WebAssembly AOT deployment remain pending acceptance work. ## Alternatives Considered | Alternative | Assessment | |---|---| | **Annotate the existing constructor** | **Recommended.** Uses the standard immutable-type mechanism and preserves the existing JSON shape. | | Framework converter preserving the object shape | Technically possible, but adds parsing/writing and option-handling code that the built-in constructor binding already provides. Reserve for a demonstrated requirement the annotation cannot meet. | | Application-registered object-shaped converter | Valid opt-in workaround when an application cannot upgrade and must retain `MarkupString` in its model. Requires implementation and registration at each relevant serialization boundary; not the preferred framework fix. | | Framework converter using a bare JSON string | A different wire contract that could invalidate existing object-shaped payloads. Applications may opt into their own representation; it is not needed for this issue. | | Store a `string` in the application DTO and reconstruct `MarkupString` afterward | Simple workaround when the DTO contract can change; mapping to a string can change the wire shape unless a nested DTO preserves it. Not a framework fix. | | Application contract/resolver customization | Possible depending on the contract and serializer version, but advanced and application-owned. A parameterless `CreateObject` callback alone cannot bind incoming content to the immutable value. | | Add a writable or init-only `Value` accessor | Expands the public surface and changes immutable construction conventions unnecessarily. | | Add `[JsonInclude]` to `Value` only | Does not provide a setter or select the string constructor; not sufficient on its own. | | No framework change | Possible if maintainers decline the default-behavior compatibility change; affected applications retain mapping or custom-serialization workarounds. | ## Validation Plan The following is implementation acceptance work, not a record of executed tests. ### Faithful regression boundary - **Behavior owner:** `MarkupString` constructor metadata together with `System.Text.Json` contract construction. - **Production producer:** The real serializer operating on the actual Components type, including generated metadata for that type. - **Final observable:** Exact restored `.Value` and unchanged parsed JSON structure. - **Permanent surface:** The existing Components managed test project, extending a matching type-specific class if present and following the area's naming and xUnit conventions. - **False-pass risk:** Surrogate types, converters, manual reconstruction, `ToString()`-only checks, or generated serialization without generated deserialization do not establish the regression fix. ### Acceptance criteria 1. Reproduce the issue against the then-current default branch with the actual issue DTO and framework type, after activating the repository SDK and inspecting relevant history and documentation. 2. Non-empty, empty, and Unicode strings round-trip both directly and inside the DTO under default and web naming options. Every value-preservation regression row fails for the expected lost-value reason without the annotation and passes with it; inspect each parameterized result. 3. Parsed serialized JSON before and after the change has the same object shape and appropriate `Value` member. Do not assert one HTML escaping spelling. 4. Generated metadata serializes and deserializes the real framework type using generated `JsonTypeInfo` overloads in a validation consumer with reflection fallback disabled. 5. Execute the edge-case compatibility matrix with explicit option values. Controls for null/default, missing members, strict options, invalid types, top-level strings, and nullable/non-nullable JSON null need not fail on baseline. 6. One representative collection-value case and one application-converter precedence case pass. 7. Existing construction, conversion, `ToString()`, and markup-rendering tests remain green. Run affected builds and API checks; update tracked API metadata only if tooling requires it. 8. Follow the Components sample workflow with representative Server and WebAssembly hosts that actually serialize/restore and expose the value. Rendering alone is not evidence. Preserve browser-owned assertions in the established Selenium suite when required, then remove temporary probes. 9. If claiming trimmed deployment, publish and run a trimmed consumer. If claiming Native AOT or browser WebAssembly AOT, publish and execute each claimed path separately. 10. Record commands, revisions, effective options, relevant switches, per-case results, and any unverified boundaries. Managed serializer tests are the primary regression proof; host smoke coverage does not replace them. Do not expand this annotation-only proposal into a render-mode, navigation, reconnect, or streaming matrix unless implementation touches or claims those paths. **Execution status:** No runtime reproduction, framework build, generated-context execution, browser validation, or publish validation has been performed for this design proposal. ## Documentation Plan - Add a concise consumer-facing API remark/example explaining object-shaped JSON support and reading `.Value` after deserialization. - Document naming, ignore settings, strict options, and application converter limitations; link to existing serializer documentation rather than duplicating a general guide. - Record intentional compatibility differences and the maintainer's release decision in issue/PR notes and any required release notes. - Update API-review material and tracked metadata only as required by repository tooling. ## Evidence and Analysis Boundary - The original analysis recorded one automated triage comment on the originating issue and no matches from an issue-number PR search. These are historical observations, not a current issue-state check or proof that no unlinked work exists. - The original analysis recorded local commit `c036f431d5078d8c60985b6730925cbf4908b2d2`, upstream snapshot `0fe823627dddb94849b8a737b547b14dff2f46ca`, and shared source blob `d88c2e7b4c3cd9592e442c8ac407cf466fea212f`. These historical revision/hash claims were not independently revalidated in this revision. - The prior document review inspected local `MarkupString.cs` and confirmed the constructor/getter shape and absence of the attribute. This does not verify upstream's then-current default branch. - The original test inventory reported markup-rendering coverage and no dedicated `MarkupStringTest.cs`. Recheck the current test surface before selecting a permanent class. - Official serializer documentation supports the proposed mechanism; source/documentation analysis is not runtime or red/green verification. - The reference proposal and its maintainer comment were read for this revision. Its structure is reused, not its feature-specific implementation claims or approval status. ## References - [Structure reference: dotnet/aspnetcore#67848](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67848). - [Maintainer response on the reference proposal](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67848#issuecomment-5006356571). - [Originating issue and requested constructor annotation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67608). - [Upstream MarkupString source at the inspected revision](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/0fe823627dddb94849b8a737b547b14dff2f46ca/src/Components/Components/src/MarkupString.cs). - [System.Text.Json immutable types and parameterized constructors](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/standard/serialization/system-text-json/immutability). - [Required constructor parameters](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/standard/serialization/system-text-json/required-properties#non-optional-constructor-parameters). - [Nullable-annotation enforcement](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/standard/serialization/system-text-json/nullable-annotations). - [Source-generation modes](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/standard/serialization/system-text-json/source-generation-modes).

Issues.Title: Do not emit or traverse non-security-enabled groups in Negotiate LDAP claims
Issues.Body:
- [x] You've read the [Contributor Guide](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).
- [x] You've included unit or integration tests for your change, where applicable.
- [x] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [x] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making. If you'd like to propose a new feature or change, please open an issue to discuss the change or find an existing issue.

Do not emit or traverse non-security-enabled groups in Negotiate LDAP claims

## Description

When `EnableLdap` is used, group memberships are resolved by following `memberOf` links. Active Directory computes the Windows token over security-enabled groups only, so a group that is not security-enabled (a distribution group) is not part of the expansion and nothing is reachable through it. The LDAP path did not make that distinction.

This change makes `LdapAdapter` consistent with that model:

* Every group, direct or nested, is resolved through `GetGroups` (renamed from `GetNestedGroups`), including when `IgnoreNestedGroups` is `true`. In that mode only the recursion is skipped, not the group check.
* `groupType` is requested in the existing base-scope read, so there is no additional LDAP round trip.
* A group that is not security-enabled produces no role claim and its `memberOf` links are not followed.
* A missing or unparsable `groupType` (non-Active Directory servers) fails open, so behavior there is unchanged. The bit test is done in C# rather than with the AD-specific bitwise matching rule.
* The AppContext switch `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate.AllowNonSecurityEnabledGroupClaims` restores the previous behavior (emit and traverse every group). It is read once into a static field.
* The omission is logged at `Debug`.

This is the same behavior that is already in `release/8.0` and `release/9.0`, plus the traversal change on top, so `main` and `release/10.0` currently lack the `groupType` handling this PR depends on. Because of that this PR contains the forward port and the traversal change together.

One behavior to be aware of: a group whose entry no longer exists (stale `memberOf` reference) no longer produces a role claim, because the claim is now added after the group is read. This matches the release branches.

### Tests

`GetGroups` is exercised through a `LdapConnection` subclass that overrides `SendRequest`. The `System.DirectoryServices.Protocols` response types have no public constructors, so responses are built reflectively in one helper. The new tests cover:

* distribution group: not emitted, parents not traversed
* security group: emitted, parents traversed
* security group reachable only through a distribution group: not emitted
* opt-out switch: emitted and traversed
* missing `groupType`: emitted and traversed
* `IgnoreNestedGroups` both values
* `IsSecurityGroup` and `ShouldEmitRoleClaim` value matrices

Validation on this branch:

* `dotnet test src\Security\Authentication\Negotiate\test\Negotiate.Test\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate.Test.csproj`: Passed 96, Failed 0.
* With only the traversal `return;` removed, exactly 2 tests fail (`GetGroups_DistributionGroup_IsNotEmittedAndItsParentsAreNotTraversed` and `GetGroups_SecurityGroupBehindADistributionGroup_IsNotReached`), with the extra role leaking, and the other tests still pass. The behavior was also checked end to end against a Samba AD domain controller.

Fixes #69953

Issues.Title: Negotiate LDAP: do not traverse parents of groups that are not security-enabled
Issues.Body:
## Summary

When Negotiate resolves LDAP group memberships into role claims, it stops emitting a role for a group that is not security-enabled, but it still follows that group's own `memberOf` links. Groups reachable only through such a group can therefore still become role claims. This breaks the invariant that only security-enabled groups, and groups reachable through security-enabled groups, confer roles.

## What is wrong

* Active Directory computes a user's effective group set (the `tokenGroups` expansion) over security-enabled groups only. A group that is not security-enabled (a distribution group) is not a vertex in that graph, so nothing is reachable through it. This is specified in MS-DRSR 4.1.8.3 (`IDL_DRSGetMemberships`), with `IsMatchedGroup` in 4.1.8.2.6 requiring `GROUP_TYPE_SECURITY_ENABLED`, and `Closure` in 4.1.8.2.2 requiring every intermediate vertex to be in the filtered set.
* `LdapAdapter.GetGroups` applies the `groupType` check only to the decision of whether to emit the group's own claim. The recursion into the group's `memberOf` is not gated by that decision.
* As a result the LDAP path and the Windows token disagree about which groups a user effectively belongs to when a distribution group is nested inside a security group.

## Why it matters (defense in depth)

* Correctness: the role set produced on the LDAP path should not be larger than the set a Windows token would carry for the same user. Documentation maps Windows Authentication security groups to application roles.
* Hardening: nesting a distribution group into a security group is permitted by the directory without warning and has no effect on Windows access, so such nestings are rarely audited. Treating them as authorization-bearing only in this component widens the role set silently.
* Distribution lists are often built from security groups and are often managed by different people than the security groups they end up nested in, so the delegation boundary of each should be respected.

## Affected code

* src/Security/Authentication/Negotiate/src/Internal/LdapAdapter.cs:147-202 - `GetGroups`: the claim decision (line 172) and the recursion over `memberOf` (line 186 onward) are independent
* src/Security/Authentication/Negotiate/src/Internal/LdapAdapter.cs:122-124 - `RetrieveClaimsAsync` call site; nesting is resolved through `GetGroups` in both nesting modes
* src/Security/Authentication/Negotiate/src/Internal/LdapAdapter.cs:304-305 - `ShouldEmitRoleClaim`, the existing predicate combining the `groupType` check and the compatibility switch

Line numbers refer to `release/9.0`, where the `groupType` handling already exists.

## Recommended fix

Return from `GetGroups` in the branch where `ShouldEmitRoleClaim` is false, so that a group that is not emitted is also not traversed. This mirrors the directory's own expansion, where such a group is not part of the graph. No new LDAP round trip is needed, because `groupType` is already read for each group.

The existing behavior is preserved where it should be:

* When `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate.AllowNonSecurityEnabledGroupClaims` is set, `ShouldEmitRoleClaim` returns true, so the group is emitted and traversed as before.
* When `groupType` is absent (non-Active Directory servers), `IsSecurityGroup` returns true, so the group is emitted and traversed as before.

Alternatives considered:

* A separate predicate such as `ShouldTraverseNestedGroups`: rejected because it duplicates the decision and can drift from `ShouldEmitRoleClaim`.
* Filtering with the AD bitwise matching rule in the LDAP query: rejected because it is Active Directory specific and returns nothing on other servers, whereas the C# check fails open.
* Reading the `tokenGroups` constructed attribute: a possible larger redesign, but it changes the query shape and is out of scope for a hardening fix.

Compatibility: this is a behavior change for directories that nest a distribution group into a security group and rely on the extra role. It is gated by the existing `AllowNonSecurityEnabledGroupClaims` switch, so the escape hatch already exists. It should be called out in release notes. The omission log line is `LogDebug`, so it is not noisy for operators.

This depends on the `groupType` handling that exists on `release/8.0` and `release/9.0` and is not yet on `main`, so the change on `main` must include it or follow its forward port.

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] A group that is not security-enabled is neither emitted as a role nor traversed to its parents.
* [ ] A security-enabled group is emitted and traversed.
* [ ] A security group reachable only through a non-security-enabled group is not emitted.
* [ ] With `AllowNonSecurityEnabledGroupClaims` set, non-security-enabled groups are emitted and traversed as before.
* [ ] A missing `groupType` attribute keeps emitting and traversing.
* [ ] The behavior holds with `IgnoreNestedGroups` both true and false.
* [ ] Unit tests drive `GetGroups` through a `LdapConnection` subclass overriding `SendRequest`, with responses built in a single test helper.
* [ ] The behavior change and the compatibility switch are documented.

Issues.Title: Add the openharmony RIDs and skip repo-side NativeAOT for openharmony
Issues.Body:
### Summary

Add `openharmony-arm64`/`openharmony-x64` to the shared-framework supported
RIDs, the explicit runtime/crossgen2 package list, and the bundled-tool RIDs.
Skip repo-side NativeAOT for openharmony: the repository's bundled tools and
E2E AOT harnesses do not have the OpenHarmony cross-AOT toolchain wired up.
This does not affect user AOT publishing, which uses the runtime ILCompiler
pack.

### Changes

- `Directory.Build.props`: add the two openharmony RIDs to
  `SupportedRuntimeIdentifiers`, and set `NativeAotSupported=false` when the
  target OS or runtime identifier is openharmony (repo-side tools and E2E
  harnesses only).
- `Directory.Packages.props`: add `Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.openharmony-*`
  and `Microsoft.NETCore.App.Crossgen2.openharmony-*` to the explicit runtime
  package list.
- `src/Tools/Directory.Build.props`: add the openharmony RIDs to
  `BundledToolTargetRuntimeIdentifiers`.
- `src/Components/Testing/testassets/NativeAotTestApp/NativeAotTestApp.csproj`
  and `.../PackageConsumer/App/PackageConsumer.App.csproj`: skip `PublishAot`
  for openharmony in the E2E AOT harnesses.
- Five files, 17 insertions and 4 deletions.

### Impact

- OpenHarmony only; other platforms keep their RID lists and NativeAOT setup.
- The shared framework is produced with crossgen2 and is unchanged. NativeAOT
  is skipped only for the repository's own tools and E2E harnesses; user AOT
  publishing is served by the runtime ILCompiler pack.
- The RIDs come from the runtime RID graph added in dotnet/runtime#132953.

### Follow-up

Repo-side AOT for openharmony can be enabled once the runtime ILCompiler pack
for the pinned version and the OpenHarmony cross-AOT toolchain (NDK/lld, see
the prereqs image discussion) are available to the build.

### Test

1. Build for `openharmony-arm64`: the shared framework and bundled tools
   resolve the openharmony RIDs; repo-side NativeAOT is not attempted.
2. The E2E AOT harnesses skip `PublishAot` on openharmony.
3. CI runs the regular build/test legs for the change.

> [!NOTE]
> This PR was authored with AI assistance (agent tooling) under the author's direction.

Issues.Title: Make Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebView trim/NativeAOT compatible
Issues.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/69946
Related: https://github.com/dotnet/maui/issues/38121#issuecomment-5511865798

## Description

`Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebView` couldn't run when trimmed or published with NativeAOT. Under the AOT default (`JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault=false`) the very first IPC message from the page (`AttachPage`) throws `InvalidOperationException: Reflection-based serialization has been disabled`. Even with reflection re-enabled, `JsonElement[]`, enum and `NavigationOptions` converters are missing native code, and root component constructors are trimmed away. This blocks Blazor Hybrid hosts built on AOT-friendly WebView bindings.

**Downstream impact:** callers that pass an unannotated `Type` to `WebViewManager.AddRootComponentAsync` with the trim analyzer enabled will now get IL2067/IL2072. This includes MAUI's `RootComponent.ComponentType` (`src/BlazorWebView/src/Maui/RootComponent.cs`, whose project sets `EnableTrimAnalyzer=true`). The fix there is to add `[DynamicallyAccessedMembers(DynamicallyAccessedMemberTypes.All)]` to `ComponentType`. That code is already incorrect under trimming today (the constructor can be trimmed away); the warning makes it visible. I'm happy to send the matching dotnet/maui PR.

Out of scope: reflection-based paths in `Microsoft.JSInterop` and `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web` (user-defined interop argument/result types, event args). They still produce their own trim/AOT warnings, but they no longer prevent the WebView channel itself from working.

### Validation

- `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebView.Test`: 36/36 pass. 16 are existing tests, which also exercise `BeginInvokeJS`/`AttachToDocument`/`RenderBatch` through the new serializer. The 20 new tests are in `IpcCommonTest`: wire-format equality with the previous implementation, round-trips, prefix handling, and the unsupported-type error. Temporarily removing the camelCase policy from the context makes the equality and round-trip tests fail, so they do catch format drift.
- **Analyzers:** with only `IsTrimmable=true` applied to the original code, the build fails with IL2026/IL3050 in `IpcCommon.Serialize`/`TryDeserialize` and IL2067 in `WebViewRenderer.AddRootComponent`. With this change it builds with 0 warnings.
- The other projects that reference WebView (`Samples/PhotinoPlatform`, `test/StaticWebAssets`) build with 0 warnings. I couldn't run the StaticWebAssets tests locally: they build apps from locally packed packages under paths longer than Windows' MAX_PATH on my machine, so they rely on CI here.
- **`src/Tools/LinkabilityChecker`** passes with WebView included (ILLink `--action link` over all trimmable projects, 0 warnings).
- **End to end, NativeAOT and trimmed:** a console app in the `eng/testing/linker` harness shape (same support files and template, `TrimMode=full`, reflection-based JSON off), referencing WebView via `ProjectReference`. It plays the role of `blazor.webview.js` against a minimal `WebViewManager` and checks `AttachPage` → `BeginInvokeJS` + `AttachToDocument` + `RenderBatch` → root component constructed and rendered → `OnRenderCompleted` → `NavigationManager.NavigateTo` → `Navigate`.

The same app was published both with NativeAOT and trimmed-only (`PublishTrimmed=true`, `TrimMode=full`, ILLink, JIT runtime):

| | NativeAOT: WebView warnings | NativeAOT: result | Trimmed: WebView warnings | Trimmed: result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `main` | 8 | `AttachPage` fails (reflection-based serialization disabled); nothing after it works | 3 | same failure |
| this PR | 0 | all steps pass, exit code 100 | 0 | all steps pass, exit code 100 |

I didn't add this as a `*.NativeAotTests` project. The harness only supports extra references via the `$(LibrariesProjectRoot)X\src\X.csproj` pattern, which WebView's path doesn't fit, and `TreatWarningsAsErrors` would trip on the remaining JSInterop/Components.Web warnings. I'm happy to add it (with a small `trimmingTests.targets` change) if you'd like it in this PR.

Issues.Title: Fix malformed default URL for Blazor WebAssembly B2C instance
Issues.Body:
# Correct the default URL displayed for the Blazor WebAssembly B2C instance.

## Description

Running `dotnet new blazorwasm --help` displays the following malformed default for `--aad-b2c-instance`:

`https:////aadB2CInstance.b2clogin.com/`

The expected default is:

`https://aadB2CInstance.b2clogin.com/`

### Root cause

The `AAdB2CInstance` template parameter defines a four-slash `replaces` marker but does not define an explicit `defaultValue`. Consequently, the template engine exposes the replacement marker as the parameter's default in CLI help.

The marker matches the placeholder in the template's source configuration. Changing it directly would break that correspondence.

### Solution

Add an explicit `defaultValue` of `https://aadB2CInstance.b2clogin.com/`, following the existing pattern used by the adjacent `AADInstance` parameter.

Keep the four-slash `replaces` marker and source placeholder unchanged so template substitution continues to work.

### Test coverage

Add an integration regression test that uses the existing template-package installer and runs `dotnet new blazorwasm --help` against locally built templates in an isolated hive. The test verifies:

- The command exits successfully.
- The displayed default contains the correctly formatted B2C URL.
- The malformed four-slash URL is absent.
- Whitespace and terminal line wrapping between `Default:` and the URL
  do not cause a false failure.

Fixes #44894

Issues.Title: Prevent stale layout Body reuse without clearing page defaults
Issues.Body: ## Description When navigating from a child page to a page that also serves as its layout, the routed page can reuse the layout component instance. The retained `Body` then renders the parent page recursively, causing duplicate content. This change gives routed `LayoutComponentBase` pages distinct render-tree identities according to whether route values explicitly supply `Body`. It prevents a layout instance from being reused as the routed page, while preserving constructor-initialized `Body` content on a fresh page. ## Root Cause `RouteView` rendered the routed component without an identity boundary. When the renderer reused a component instance that had been acting as a layout, the omitted `Body` route parameter left the previous layout body in place. Unconditionally passing `Body = null` fixes that transition but also overwrites a constructor-initialized body on first arrival. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2dfed66-cfec-4a13-964b-51fa1dee88b7 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c233c26-a309-4f4e-a88f-62044b952ff0 ## After Fix Routed layout pages with an explicit `Body` value and those without one receive separate identities. This prevents stale layout state from carrying over, while a new page retains its constructor-provided default. Regression tests cover the layout-to-page transition, returning to the child layout, constructor-initialized `Body`, and explicit/omitted `Body` values including case-insensitive parameter names. ## Testing - `dotnet test src\Components\Components\test\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Tests.csproj --no-restore --filter "FullyQualifiedName~RouteViewTest" -p:UseIisNativeAssets=false -v:q` — passed (12/12). - `dotnet build src\Components\test\E2ETest\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.E2ETests.csproj --no-restore -v:q -p:UseIisNativeAssets=false` — passed. - The filtered Selenium routing tests did not reach their assertions because Chrome crashed on startup (`DevToolsActivePort file doesn't exist`). Interactive Playwright validation was also unavailable because the Playwright MCP server could not authenticate to npm. Real-browser behavior remains unverified in this environment. Fixes #69900

Issues.Title: OpenAPI: `required` is not emitted for properties of a `[FromForm]` complex type in MVC controllers
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

When an MVC controller action binds a complex type with `[FromForm]`, the generated OpenAPI document never includes a `required` list for the form schema — `[BindRequired]` and `[Required]` on the model's properties are ignored.

At runtime those properties are still enforced by model binding/validation, so the document describes the fields as optional while the server rejects requests that omit them (400). Client generators (e.g. NSwag, Kiota) then produce optional/nullable parameters for fields that are actually required.

The same fields declared as separate action parameters are correctly marked as `required`, so this looks like a gap left by #57196 (fix for #57112 / #57712), which handles requiredness only for non-exploded form parameters.

```csharp
[ApiController]
[Route("upload")]
public class UploadController : ControllerBase
{
    [HttpPost("dto")]
    [Consumes("multipart/form-data")]
    public IActionResult UploadDto([FromForm] UploadRequest request) => Ok();

    [HttpPost("params")]
    [Consumes("multipart/form-data")]
    public IActionResult UploadParams(
        [FromForm, BindRequired] long documentId,
        [FromForm, Required] string name,
        [Required] IFormFile file) => Ok();
}

public sealed class UploadRequest
{
    [BindRequired] public long DocumentId { get; init; }
    [Required] public string Name { get; init; } = null!;
    [Required] public IFormFile File { get; init; } = null!;
}
```

Generated schema for `POST /upload/dto` — no `required`:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "DocumentId": { "pattern": "^-?(?:0|[1-9]\\d*)$", "type": ["integer", "string"], "format": "int64" },
    "Name": { "type": "string" },
    "File": { "$ref": "#/components/schemas/IFormFile" }
  }
}
```

Generated schema for `POST /upload/params` — `required` is present:

```json
{
  "required": ["documentId", "name", "file"],
  "type": "object",
  "allOf": [ ... ]
}
```

Yet a request to `/upload/dto` without `DocumentId` is rejected:

```
curl -F Name=a -F File=@f.txt http://localhost:5000/upload/dto

HTTP 400
{"title":"One or more validation errors occurred.","status":400,
 "errors":{"DocumentId":["A value for the 'DocumentId' parameter or property was not provided."]}}
```


### Expected Behavior

Properties of a `[FromForm]` complex type that are required by model binding/validation (`[BindRequired]`, `[Required]`) should be listed in `required` of the form schema, consistent with how separate form parameters are handled:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["DocumentId", "Name", "File"],
  "properties": { ... }
}
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a new `web` project targeting `net10.0` and add `Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi` 10.0.13.
2. Register `AddControllers()`, `AddOpenApi()`, `MapControllers()`, `MapOpenApi()`.
3. Add the controller and model from above.
4. Open `/openapi/v1.json` and compare the `multipart/form-data` schemas of `/upload/dto` and `/upload/params`.


### Exceptions (if any)

_No response_

### .NET Version

10.0.401 (Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi 10.0.13)

### Anything else?

In `OpenApiDocumentService.GetFormRequestBody`, MVC-exploded parameters (`ModelMetadata.ContainerType is not null`) go through the `else` branch, which only adds entries to `Properties` and never calls `IsRequired(description)`:

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/d4dfec9fffae3cfbb9b5f60b4613273ea130a2b1/src/OpenApi/src/Services/OpenApiDocumentService.cs#L679-L699

Note that `IsRequired(ApiParameterDescription)` alone may not be enough for this branch: `ApiParameterDescription.IsRequired` reflects `[BindRequired]`, but `[Required]` on a model property is only visible via `ModelMetadata.ValidatorMetadata` (the existing check looks at `ParameterInfo` attributes of the action parameter, i.e. the container).

As a workaround we use an operation transformer that fills `schema.Required` from `ModelMetadata.IsBindingRequired` / `RequiredAttribute` in `ModelMetadata.ValidatorMetadata`.

Related: #57112, #57712, #57082, #57196, #68147.

Issues.Title: Clarify rate-limiter ordering with `UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute`
Issues.Body:
Endpoint-specific rate-limit policies are not applied to a re-executed endpoint when `UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute` is registered after `UseRateLimiter`.

For example, with this ordering:

```csharp
    app.UseRouting();
    app.UseRateLimiter();
    app.UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute("/b");
```

A request that produces an unhandled error response can be re-executed to `/b` without running the rate limiter for `/b`, even if that endpoint's rate-limit policy has no permits remaining.

## Cause

Status-code re-execution runs routing again, followed by the middleware registered after the status-code-pages middleware. In this configuration, the rate limiter is outside that branch, so it does not evaluate the newly selected endpoint.

This is an ordering consequence rather than a failure within the rate limiter. When invoked again, the rate limiter reads the current endpoint and acquires a fresh lease.

## Documented ordering

Register status-code-pages middleware before routing, and the rate limiter after routing:

```csharp
    app.UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute("/b");
    app.UseRouting();
    app.UseRateLimiter();
```

With this ordering, re-execution includes the rate limiter, allowing it to evaluate `/b`'s policy and reject the request when no permits remain.

## Suggested improvement

Explicitly document this interaction in the rate-limiting and status-code-pages guidance, with an ordering example and a note that middleware placed before status-code-pages middleware does not run again during re-execution.

Issues.Title: Identity API `/manage/2fa` returns success when a concurrent update prevents saving changes
Issues.Body:
The `/manage/2fa` endpoint registered by `MapIdentityApi` can return HTTP 200 with two-factor authentication settings that were not persisted. A user's own concurrent activity can trigger this, causing an authenticator-key reset to appear successful even though the previous key remains stored.

In `src/Identity/Core/src/IdentityApiEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions.cs`, the handler ignores the `IdentityResult` returned by `SetTwoFactorEnabledAsync` and `ResetAuthenticatorKeyAsync`. If a concurrent update to the same user causes an EF Core concurrency conflict, the update fails but the tracked user entity retains its modified values. The handler then builds `TwoFactorResponse` from that entity, potentially returning an authenticator key that does not match the stored key.

## Reproduction

Reported as reproduced on ASP.NET Core 10.0.12.

1. Submit a `/manage/2fa` request with `resetSharedKey: true`.
2. Concurrently update the same user so that the reset encounters a concurrency conflict.
3. Observe HTTP 200 with a new shared key, while the database retains the previous key.
4. Attempt to enable 2FA using a code generated from the returned key; the request fails with `400 InvalidTwoFactorCode`.

## Expected behavior

Failed updates should be surfaced as errors rather than returning success with unpersisted settings.

## Suggested fix

- Check `IdentityResult.Succeeded` for every `SetTwoFactorEnabledAsync` and `ResetAuthenticatorKeyAsync` call, including the reset used to initialize a missing key, and return a validation error on failure.
- Treat a `null` result from `GenerateNewTwoFactorRecoveryCodesAsync` as a failure rather than returning HTTP 200 with `RecoveryCodes = null`.

Issues.Title: Remember me isPersistent understanding
Issues.Body:
This is more of a question but its not enough of a question that i could post it up on stack overflow without risking it just getting closed as primary opinion based or to broad.   So i am going to put it here in hopes of getting an answer.

The issue is the understanding of how remember me is supposed to work.    My problem is that its not doing what we would expect it to do.   

Management expects when a user logs in and clicks remember me that they will then not be required to type their login and password again for a month.  Whether or not they will still have to type in the 2fa code is up for debate.

What is actually happening is that i can close the browser reboot and come back for about an hour and 15 minutes and then i will be forced to type my password again.    This still happens even with a valid `.AspNetCore.Identity.Application` cookie set that is not due to expire for another month.

After digging around in the code i found that Remember me is actually isPersistent and it is defined as.

>Flag indicating whether the sign-in cookie should persist after the browser is closed.

Which brings you to:

There are two different types of Cookies:

- session cookies, held in memory, and which expire once the browser exits
- persistent cookies, which have a time-to-live, are persisted on disk, and are sent by the browser until their time-to-live has elapsed.

All this being said remember machine 2fa works as expected i am not prompted again for the 2fa and i have a cookie on my machine `Identity.TwoFactorRememberMe`.

So I guess my question is why are we not getting a `Identity.FactorRememberMe` or why isn't sign in respecting a long life time of the `AspNetCore.Identity.Application` cookie?

How is this supposed to work exactly?   I am following the code here even though we have normal MVC and not razor pages like you have in the example.  I am still just calling 

>var signInUserResult = await _signInManager.PasswordSignInAsync(userName, password, rememberMe, true);

Note: I am using Asp .net Identity in Identity server 4 application.

Issues.Title: Should IdentityUser be in the EntityFramework namespace?
Issues.Body:
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.identity.entityframeworkcore.identityuser?view=aspnetcore-1.1

I'm looking through various implementations from the [readme](https://github.com/aspnet/Identity/blob/master/README.md) and I've noticed they all use `IdentityUser ` for their concrete type to pass to `UserManager`, or have had to craft a custom type to be able to have a contract between the database and the .NET AspNetIdentity implentation they've written (see the DynamoDB library).

I've had to do this too for the [Marten implementation I've written](https://github.com/yetanotherchris/Marten.AspNetIdentity), and the reason is, a `TUser` that your `UserStore` takes, should really be an interface - it will always have an email, most likely an Id of some sort, firstname, lastname and then a bag of properties.

Things become even more abstract when dealing with claims.

If everyone is using `IdentityUser` or their own custom `TUser` doesn't this defeat the purpose of AspnetIdentity - which is to be able to switch and change implementations easily? That isn't possible if your consumer is tightly coupled with a `TUser` implementation of the library.

### Example `TUser` implementations

- [MongoIdentityUser](https://github.com/tugberkugurlu/AspNetCore.Identity.MongoDB/blob/master/src/AspNetCore.Identity.MongoDB/MongoIdentityUser.cs)
- [DynamoIdentityUser](https://github.com/miltador/AspNetCore.Identity.DynamoDB/blob/master/src/AspNetCore.Identity.DynamoDB/DynamoIdentityUser.cs)
- [Redis uses `IdentityUser<string>`](https://github.com/aguacongas/Identity.Redis/blob/develop/src/Aguacongas.Identity.Redis/UserStore.cs)
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Should IdentityUser be in the EntityFramework namespace?" (#2056)

Issues.Body:
Apologize if my feedback may sound controversial or may spark a debate.

I need to be sure that the problem mentioned on this [page](https://github.com/aspnet/Tooling/blob/master/known-issues-vs2017.md#to-create-aspnet-core-10--11-projects-install-visual-studios-net-core-10---11-developer-tools-for-web-component) about .NET Core 1.0/1.1 tooling is installed when creating new ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 project should not happen or should not be supported in VS 2019.

These are my main concerns:

1. VS 2019 is about to be released in around early 2019
2. ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 is not going to be supported anymore, based on [this page](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/master/microsoft-support.md).
3. Creating new ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 will always install the .NET Core 1.0/1.1 web tooling, and this is not necessary when previous reason has reached the unsupported period and it's quite near or might be the same time of VS 2019 release.
4. Based on the problem mentioned above, VS 2017 has no "built in" tooling when creating new ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 project, but the external tooling may help. Therefore for those that still need to maintain ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 projects, we could use VS 2017 as long as the VS 2017 is still in support lifecycle or in mainstream support lifecycle.

I welcome feedback 🙂

Issues.Title: Support dotnet watch in launchSettings.json
Issues.Body:
I used to be able to use `dotnet watch` in Visual Studio by adding the following section to `launchSettings.json` and starting the project without debugging using CTRL + F5.

```
    "Kestrel (dotnet watch run)": {
      "commandName": "Executable",
      "executablePath": "C:\\Program Files\\dotnet\\dotnet.exe",
      "commandLineArgs": "watch run",
      "launchBrowser": true,
      "launchUrl": "https://localhost:5001/",
      "environmentVariables": {
        "ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT": "Development"
      }
    },
```

This used to work in ASP.NET Core 1.1 but no longer does. According to https://github.com/aspnet/DotNetTools/issues/404 the new format for ASP.NET Core 2.0 is:

```
   "Kestrel (dotnet watch run)": {
      "commandName": "Executable",
      "executablePath": "C:\\Program Files\\dotnet\\dotnet.exe",
      "commandLineArgs": "watch run",
      "workingDirectory": "C:\\Users\\namc\\source\\repos\\WebApplication2\\WebApplication2",
      "launchBrowser": true,
      "launchUrl": "https://localhost:5001/",
      "environmentVariables": {
        "ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT": "Development"
      }
    }
```

The problem with this is the hard coded `executablePath` which is Windows specific and the `workingDirectory` which is specific to wherever I did a Git clone on my local machine.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Support dotnet watch in launchSettings.json" (#1067)

Issues.Title: Nesting bug
Issues.Body:
The is a problem nesting embedded resources.  I was experimenting with nesting .cshtml files using the existing rules and did this:

Modal.cs (bootstrap modal web component)
   -> Modal.cs.cshtml (it's view file)

`Modal.cs.cshtml` is set to Embedded Resource, and clearly shows it, but is completed IGNORED by the build process (simply open the DLL in a text editor [such as Notepad++] and scroll to the bottom and look for text).  If I rename the file to "Modal.cshtml" instead it works perfectly fine!  :/  I don't think whether or not a file is embedded should have and role in excluding a file from being embedded so this seems like a bug to me.

Yes, I'm aware of upcoming nesting controls in v15.6, but I'm not able to install it yet, and regardless, this should work fine, so it should be looked into nonetheless.

Just to add: I'm using wild-cards to include the file.  If I explicitly add it I get this:

`Duplicate 'EmbeddedResource' items were included. ...`
